descriptions.text: The Mure Distribution contract's distribute function moves tokens from a victim to an arbitrary recipient based on a Distribution struct plus a signer/signature, but it let the caller supply the signer address and validated the signature via ERC-1271 against that caller-controlled signer. The attacker deployed a malicious contract that (a) implements isValidSignature to always return the ERC-1271 magic value, (b) implements supportsInterface/poolState to masquerade as a legitimate Mure pool/source, and passed itself as both source and signer. With validation thus self-satisfied, the attacker called distribute to pull 4,848,683,803,036 QUEST from the victim (who had granted allowance to the distributor) into the attacker contract, then routed QUEST -> USDC -> WETH via Uniswap V3 and unwrapped to ~5.45 ETH. The root cause is that signature/pool verification trusted attacker-supplied contracts instead of binding to a fixed trusted signer. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xb83040361a0ec72fa2d06ad69493226518a5f8b5d96c19b400626248f9c5b798 Analysis: https://x.com/DefimonAlerts/status/2058211424761942226

Mure’s MureDistribution proxy contract on Ethereum was exploited due to an access control vulnerability in signature validation. The attacker supplied a malicious contract as the “signer source,” causing SignatureChecker to return true and bypass verification. This allowed draining 4.85M QUEST tokens (pre-approved to the proxy) via transferFrom, which were then swapped for ~5.45 ETH (~$11,700) on Uniswap. No user funds or main payment infrastructure were affected; it was a targeted logic flaw in one distribution contract.

The MureDistribution contract on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited on 21 May 2026, allowing an attacker to drain approximately 4.85 million QUEST tokens, worth about $11,700, from an externally approved wallet. The attacker circumvented signature verification by supplying an attacker-controlled contract as both the source and the verifier, exploiting the contract's reliance on user-supplied data for authorization. The contract based signature verification and the authoritative signer identity on a user-supplied contract.
